* Added in the second session
** Guitar voice-led triads
Two guitar voicing styles in voicings.js, both three notes on ONE string set, each chord taking the
shape whose strings move least from the one before (ChordVoicings.lead):
- =triadvl= root-3rd-5th of every chord (a 7th chord gives its plain triad).
- =uppervl= the triad on the 3rd of a 7th chord (3-5-7), 6-R-3 for a 6th chord, b7-9-4 for a 7sus.
The band plays them on strings 4-3-2 up to fret 12 (GUITAR_SETS in harmony.js). The Chord Sheet has a
menu item per string set; a shape picked by hand is kept and the chords after it follow.
Known: through a cycle of fourths (ii-V-I-VI) the nearest shape is always the next one UP, so the
line climbs the neck until it hits fret 12 and jumps back down. That is true voice leading, but it
may not be what is wanted; an alternative is to keep every chord inside one five-fret position.
** Meters
- A beat is the meter's lower note, except in 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8 (compound), where it is the dotted
  quarter: 6/8 has 2 beats, 12/8 has 4, and the tempo counts dotted quarters. BandHarmony.meterInfo
  decides; form bars, ctx and bar records carry =meter= and =compound=.
- In a compound bar x.5 is the beat's THIRD eighth (the player warps it to 2/3); x.333 needs straight:true.
- 3/4: jazz waltz (ride ding, ding-a, ding; hat foot on 2 and 3; kick on 1), bass walks three quarters.
- 6/8, 12/8: every eighth on the cymbal, kick on 1 (and 3), backbeat on 2 (and 4), whatever Feel says
  (the Feel menu is disabled). Bass walks one note per beat with pickup eighths; the riff is a shuffle.
  Comping uses the same figures as 4/4, which land on the triplet grid.
- The page has a Meter menu that re-writes the three blues presets; custom ABC keeps its own M: line.
- Notation writes compound bars in eighths (M:12/8, Q:3/8=); MIDI writes the time signature and
  converts the tempo to quarters.
- NOT done: 5/4, 7/4 and other meters still get the generic four-beat patterns cut to length; 2/2 is
  counted as two half-note beats; no 12/8-specific comping figure (repeated triplet chords); a tune
  that changes between simple and compound meter keeps one tempo number for both kinds of beat.

* Guitar: led by the hand, and two-note chords (2026-10-07, later)
- Guitar shapes used to follow each other by pitch only (ChordVoicings.nearest), which gave the right
  notes on awkward fingerings and hopped string sets. Now ChordVoicings.easiest picks the smallest move
  for the fretting hand: frets the hand shifts + half the fret change on each shared string + 0.75 per
  string picked up or dropped (handMotion); pitch motion only breaks near-ties, with a mild pull to fret 5.
  Used by the band for every guitar style and by the Chord Sheet's "Favor voice leading" on all fretted
  instruments. The weights are first guesses.
- The band remembers the grip it chose; the as-played hand-off carries it ({ strings }) so the Chord
  Sheet draws that fingering instead of the first shape with the same notes.
- =guide2=: two-note chords on string pairs 4-5, 3-4, 2-3 (3rd + 7th/6th; root + 3rd for a triad;
  4th + b7 for 7sus; root + 5th for a power chord). Chord Sheet menu: all pairs, or one pair.
Not done: a pinned voicing from the Chord Sheet has no grip on the band side, so the chord after a pin
is still chosen by pitch; "Standard" guitar shapes on the Backing Track do not exist (Chord Sheet only).

* Moving voicings, bass variation, loop shortcut (2026-10-07, last)
- Voicing movement menu (opts.voiceMove): hold / move / passing. "move" leads comping by the TOP NOTE
  (BandHarmony.toward): a held chord steps through inversions, a chord change continues the line by step,
  turning at the edge of the register. "passing" adds passing diminished chords in the "bh" style.
- Style "bh" (Drop 2, sixth-diminished): each chord read as a sixth chord (BandHarmony.sixthOf): maj -> 6,
  m7 -> 6 a minor 3rd up, dom -> m6 on the 5th (altered: m6 a semitone up), m7b5 -> m6 a minor 3rd up.
- Style "auto": per four-bar phrase from intensity / tempo / rhythm (comp.js autoStyle). With Variation on
  Strict the intensity never moves, so Auto stays on rootless (piano) or shells (guitar).
- "Major 7th chords: play as 6th chords" checkbox (opts.maj6, BandHarmony.asSixth).
- Bass variation follows the Variation menu (opts.variation; 0 = exact): walking skip notes and held notes,
  two-feel 3rds and dotted rhythm, riff relatives (climb, octave, sparse, approach), shuffle approach.
- Loop: L toggles it; first time it starts at the Start bar and the next chart click sets the end. An end
  before the start loops over the end of the form (player.setCycle(9, 1)). Click = end, Shift-click = start.
- Chord Sheet diagrams: fret label 27px in a left gutter, position dots at 3 5 7 9 12 15 17.
All probabilities and weights here are first guesses, unheard.

* Chord Sheet tidy-up and fingerings (2026-10-07)
- Preview bar (Print, Play with the band, notation button) and banjo / mandolin / vihuela are hidden
  by default; two quiet links at the bottom of the page bring them back (localStorage "chordSheetExtras").
- Add by type: one small row, root typed in (C, f#, Bb); the 12 root buttons are gone.
- Solfege, notation and chord-name options moved beside Show fingerings.
- Guitar fingers: one finger per fret from the lowest fretted note, squeezed to fit four fingers;
  barre = 1. Checked against the usual open chords, F and Bm barres, a drop 2 and a shell.
- Piano fingers: scored by natural finger spans (FINGER_SPAN) instead of fixed 1-2-3-5; left hand mirrored.
  Gives RH 135 / 125 / 135 for triad inversions and 1235 / 1245 / 1235 with the octave. LH root position
  with the octave comes out 5-3-2-1 where method books usually print 5-4-2-1.
- Two hands: root position or a low bass note = bass alone in the left hand; rootless or inverted
  four-note chord = two and two.
- Superimposed view (checkbox under the view options): up to four different chords on ONE keyboard
  (a lane per chord, after the Music Will jam cards) and ONE guitar fretboard (a colour per chord, split
  dots where chords share a note). Each chord is voice-led from the one before: nearest inversion on
  the keyboard, easiest hand move on guitar, in whatever voicing style the instrument has selected; the
  first chord is as its ordinary card shows it. Live menus: chord labels (names / Roman / numbers) and
  note labels (fingers / note names / chord tones). More than four chords: a tick row, a fifth tick
  replaces the earliest. A split dot carries one label per slice when the chords disagree (e.g. different
  fingers, chord tones). Covers every keyboard and fretted instrument (guitar, bass, ukulele, ...). Note labels
  also offer solfege (movable do from the key). A voicing picked by hand on a chord's own card (t.manual)
  is kept exactly; chords after it are led from it. Not done: printing.
- Two-hand piano fingering: a lone left-hand bass note is finger 5 and a three-note right hand spans 1 to 5
  (the first version of the span-based fingering printed 1 for the lone note and 1-2-3 for the right hand).
OPEN: bass still shows chord diagrams. Proposed replacement: a chord-tone map (root, 3rd, 5th, 7th as
single notes in one four-fret hand position, fingered) with the arpeggio in bass clef. Needs its own
drawing code because two tones can fall on one string.

* PLAN (steps 1-2 partly built 2026-10-07, see the last round): 9ths, 13ths and alterations, as options
Today: rootless voicings always add a 9th and 13th to a plain 7th chord; shells and guide tones ignore
written extensions; drop 2 / drop 3 keep the four most characteristic tones (C9 -> R-3-7-9, C13 -> 3-7-9-13);
"bh" ignores written 9/13 and only uses alterations to choose its reading; Standard keeps everything.
1. One place for the decision: BandHarmony.colour(chord, policy, nextChord) returning the chord the comping
   voices (as asSixth does now), so every style, the notation and the Chord Sheet agree.
2. Menu "Extensions": As written / Plain (strip to the 7th) / Add 9ths / Add 9ths and 13ths.
   "As written" must really mean it: rootless stops adding 9 and 13 to a bare C7 in that mode.
3. Menu "Dominant alterations": As written / b9 on dominants that resolve to a minor chord / Altered on
   dominants in turnarounds. Needs the next chord (already in ctx.nextChords).
4. Per-style behaviour, written as a table first (C9 C13 C7b9 C7#9 C7#11 C7alt Cmaj9 Cm9 Cm11 C6/9 x style)
   and printed by a test: shells and guide tones gain an optional third "colour" voice (3-7-9, 7-3-13);
   drop 2 gets a choice of which tone gives way (root or 5th); guitar shells put the extension on top;
   two-note chords stay 3rd and 7th.
5. "bh" readings for extended chords are a musical decision to make together: G9 is already Dm6; G13 and
   G7#11 have more than one accepted reading.
6. With colour on, the top-note line prefers the extension. The bass scale must follow added alterations
   (no natural 9th in the line under a b9).
7. The same two menus on the Chord Sheet, so its diagrams match what the band plays.

* Half time / double time (opts.timeFeel = "normal" | "half" | "double")
- BandHarmony.feelPart(part) wraps each part; BandPlayer and BandMidi.generate wrap every part with it and pass
  ctx.form / ctx.nextIndex. The chart, tempo, bar count, loop, stops and highlight are untouched: only what the
  part is shown (chords re-placed on a beat half or twice as long, tempo scaled) and where its events land.
  Events come back already swung at the part's own tempo, marked straight:true.
- Half time pairs bars by form index (1+2, 3+4...). An odd last bar, or starting / looping from the second bar
  of a pair, still works: the wrapper generates the whole pair and keeps the half it needs.
- Who changes: opts.timeFeelParts ("bass drums" by default, "drums", or "bass comp drums"). User correction:
  the comping does not double just because the rhythm section does, so it is left out unless asked for.
- Pinned voicings are re-keyed onto the wrapped bar numbers (pinsFor), so they are used in every mode.
- Limits: off in compound meters (6/8, 12/8); stop bars are played in normal time; wrapped comp events lose
  their `of` key so the hand-off to Chord Sheet re-voices; written-out notation of pre-swung sixteenths may
  look rough (unchecked).
- Odd-length bars in half time (3/4, 5/8, 7/8): the bar line falls in the middle of a band beat, so the second
  bar's chord is placed one chart beat EARLY (a push). Delaying it was the alternative.
- PINNED (user: "put a pin in it"): grouped meters. 5/8 and 7/8 are still counted as five / seven equal beats.
  Half time gets part of the way (two bars of 5/8 = one bar of five quarters, half as many notes), but a
  single bar felt 3+2 needs beats of unequal length, the way 6/8 already has beats of three eighths. Also
  pinned with it: force straight feel in x/8 meters, MIDI export writes 5/8 as 5/4.
- Idea not built: per-part time feel (drums in half time under a normal bass), and a time feel per style
  (the "Pop ballad" style's Half-time drum groove is really this).

* Intros (player cfg.intro / player.setIntro)
- { bars, kind: "vamp" | "last", tacet: "drums" }: bars played once after the count-in, only when play starts
  from bar 1. The parts get ordinary bar contexts (index 0..n-1, chorus 0, intro:true), so a tune's bass line
  or two-bar pattern runs through the intro. Stops and pins do not apply. Not in the bar log, so "export what
  was played" and the written-out chorus leave it out; a fresh MIDI export has no intro either.
- Page: Intro / Intro length / "Drums wait for bar 1" in the Play panel, saved with a setup. Loading plain
  changes, or a setup that does not mention them, clears intro, time feel, figure and stops.
- Song for My Father: four bars of Fm, bass figure + piano (its bossa pattern, NOT doubling the bass figure
  as on the record), drums in at the top. Length from the user (2026-10-07).
- Built with the anacrusis in mind: the intro is a play-once list of bars ahead of the form (Session.intro).
  A pickup would be one more (short) bar at the end of that list; rule still to write: the intro's last bar
  leaves room for it. The short LAST bar that balances a pickup is separate.
- Not built: an intro with its own chords; other parts sitting out; a drum fill into the top.

- When the comping is not one of the parts that change time (the default, "bass drums", and "drums"): same rhythm, different weight.
  double = each chord's first hit and the hits between the beats stay (straight, louder, short), other on-beat hits go; a bar with
  nothing between the beats gets one stab on the "and" of 2. half = chords ring to the next hit, beat 3 accented or struck again.
  "plain" in timeFeelParts ("bass drums plain", menu: "chords unchanged") switches it off. Skipped for arpeggio / passing-chord bars,
  stop bars and compound meters. Tests: t_timefeel.js, timefeel-ui.cdp.js.

* Piano ballad rewritten; blend sliders for comping rhythms -- 2026-10-08
Nothing here has been heard. User's own practice, as given: left-hand octaves on the root, right hand the triad in first inversion,
variation with 2 and 6, plus 4 and major 7 for gentle tension that resolves quickly; the three patterns "work best when combined".

  and of 2 after it, upper root on beat 3 (the "dotted" bass and the ballad kick). RH pieces: F whole chord, P top pair, T thumb, M, H.
  Piano + "standard" voicing = first inversion built here (3 5 1; 3 5 7 on seventh chords; top note 62..77 near the last, drawn to 70).
  Any other voicing style, a pin or a guitar is broken up as it stands (no left hand on guitar).

  the 3rd / major 7th under the root (10% x amount), only when a later hit of the same chord restores the chord tone. Only notes of the
  key: buildForm now puts keyPcs on every form bar (K: field, minor = natural minor). Major-7th therefore only on I and IV.

- Blend: opts.rhythmMix = { rhythm id: 0..1 } (unlisted = 0.5). Textures are chosen by weight; patterns marked mix change every bar, others
  every four bars; swing figures are weighted inside their group. Without rhythmMix the old behaviour (even, "mostly move on") is unchanged.
- Page: every rhythm in use (the menu's and the ticked ones) has a slider in the "Blend in more rhythms" list, default 50; 0 leaves it out;
  all at 0 = the menu's rhythm alone. Weights live in mixW (kept across rebuilds, saved in setups as mix). Unlock lists every rhythm there.

* Notation ahead, pattern transitions, drums that listen, follow-my-playing -- 2026-10-08
Nothing here has been heard; the microphone path has never run with a real microphone.
- Notation shows the chorus about to be played. player.js: cfg.ahead / setAhead(on) makes pump() generate one pass of the form (or loop)
  plus a bar beyond the scheduling horizon (Session.aheadBeats). Session.rewind() (via redo() on setOpts, setChoruses, setCycle, setChart,
  setTranspose) drops every bar not yet scheduled and generates it again; cfg.onRewind(barNo) tells the page. Parts keep their state
  across a rewind. Off while tempo steps are on or while following the microphone. The page turns it on only while the Notation panel
  is open; nowBar / hearing() keep played() (MIDI export, hand-off, "last chorus") to bars actually heard. The score is redrawn when
  the chorus on show changes (during the last bar of each pass) or when its bars are rewritten.
- Pattern transitions (comp.js planSpan): a blend is planned four bars at a time, one pattern at home, with at most one visitor: callback
  (bar 2 = the pattern just left, 35% after a change), foreshadowing (bar 4 = the next home, 40% before a change), or a break (bar 3 =
  another, 30% otherwise). With sliders the home is chosen by weight and zero-weight patterns never visit. Replaces "every 2 / 4 bars".
- Drums: more fills in all three sets; vary() drops a note or shifts weight so a fill does not repeat exactly; land() decides the bar
  after a fill: crash by energy (small fill 4-24%, larger 12-72%, into a chorus 45-85%), a quarter of that within four bars of the last
  crash, else an open hi-hat (30%) or just the kick. Jazz test: crashes fell from 2065 to 846 in 19200 bars.
- energy: the player gives the drums ctx.energy = half the conductor's intensity, a quarter how many bass / right-hand events the bar has,
  a quarter how loud they are (left-hand piano notes not counted).
- Follow my playing (page checkbox, Band panel): getUserMedia -> AnalyserNode RMS every 100 ms -> followFeed(dB): slow floor and ceiling,
  position between them smoothed (about 1 s up, 2.5 s down) -> player.setFollow(0..1); intensity = 0.3 arc + 0.7 level. Own
  AudioContext, analyser only (no playback), echo cancellation / AGC / noise suppression requested off. Not saved in setups.

** Meter changes inside a tune (2026-10-09)
- Already there: =TuneChart.parse= reads inline =[M:3/4]=, the chart draws the new signature, and every form bar has its own =beats= / =meter= / =compound=. All styles generate bars of the right length across changes (=tests/band/meter/t_change.js=).
- Added: form bars carry =unit=, the bar's beat against the beat of the tune's header meter (the tempo's beat). 4/4 to 7/8 = 0.5, 4/4 to 6/8 = 1.5, 6/8 to 2/4 = 0.6667. The written eighth note keeps its length. The player places events at =pos * unit=, advances by =beats * unit=, and tells the parts =tempo / unit=; =where()= and =positionAt()= still answer in the bar's own beats. =BandMidi.generate= records =tempo / unit= per bar, so the MIDI file has the right tempo events.
- Limits: the count-in, intro and ending use the first bar's meter. The Meter menu and the "half time is not available in 6/8" lock look at the header meter only. Half / double time pairs bars by form index, so a pair with different lengths is left in normal time. The band's notation writes 5/8 and 7/8 bars as 5/4 and 7/4 (as it already did for whole tunes in those meters). Tempo relations other than "the eighth stays the same" (e.g. quarter = dotted quarter) are not offered. There is no control on the page for adding a change: it is typed into the ABC as =[M:n/d]= at the start of the bar.

** Chart rows follow the ABC's lines; courtesy time signatures (2026-10-09)
- =TuneChart.parse= keeps each bar's =srcLine= and returns =srcBreaks= (bars per ABC line). The chart uses them as its rows unless the caller passes =barsPerRow= / =lineBreaks= or the ABC has =%%score-bars= / =%%score-breaks=. Every row is as wide as the longest line. A backslash at the end of a line joins it to the next. A tune on a single line of more than eight bars still gets four to a row (taken as unformatted).
- A change of meter is drawn as a one-line tag (=6/8=, class =tc-courtesy=) in the top right corner of the bar BEFORE the change, inside its barline. Only the very first bar (when there is no header) carries its own stacked signature. Bars clip their contents (=overflow:hidden=), so the tag cannot hang outside the cell.
- Tests: =tests/band/lead/lines.cdp.js= ("LINES OK"), =tests/band/meter/change.cdp.js=.
- The beat dots beside Play are rebuilt in =onBar= from the bar's own =beats= (count-in and intro bars included) and go back to the header meter when the band stops.

** ABC checks, tempo and style from the ABC, section list (2026-10-09)
- =TuneChart.parse= no longer lets an inline =[M:]= change the tune's header meter (=meterN=, =unitsPerBar= ... were the LAST meter's, which turned bar 1 of a 4/4 tune ending in 5/4 into a pickup). Each bar has =fullUnits= (what its meter holds) and =misfit= when its contents differ; =TuneChart.check(parsed)= lists them. Not flagged: the pickup, a last bar that completes it, two halves of a bar split by a repeat or double barline.

* John Prine fingerpicking -- 2026-10-10
Nothing here has been heard. Written from the commonly taught version of the pattern, not from a transcription; the user plays this
style and has not yet said how their own hand differs.
- Style =prine= was a placeholder (guitar held block chords). Now: comp =prine= on the steel guitar, bass =alt= (upright), no drums.
- comp.js =pickBar= (GRID entries marked =pick=): single notes, all marked arp. The thumb is not in the table; it plays every beat:
  root, inner string (the 4th; the 3rd under a D shape), alternate bass, inner string. Alternate bass = the fifth below the root when the
  guitar has it (C: low G, D: open A, A: open E, B7 / Bm: F# on the 6th string), else the 5th string under a 6th-string root (G, E, F:
  6-4-5-4). The table is the fingers: M / H / T = the lowest, next and top string above the thumb's.
  - =prine=: pinch on 2 and 4 with the string below on the and after (C: C . | E+C G | G . | E+C G).
  - =travis=: pinch on 1, then the and of 2, the and of 3, the and of 4. Offered in the style's Rhythm menu and blend list; not its default.
  - 3/4: thumb root, inner, inner; pinches on 2 and 3; a chord held into the next bar starts it on the alternate bass.
  - 6/8, 12/8: thumb root / alternate bass on the beats, two finger notes after each.
- The strings come from the grip of the "open" voicing style. Other guitar voicings and pins are picked by pitch (lowest, next, the rest).
  On the piano the thumb is the left hand (root below the chord and its fifth).
- Variation > 0: a pinch on the top string (25% x amount), a note between the beats left out (12%) or on the other string (18%), a pinch
  on beat 1 (15%). Strict = the pattern exactly.
** VERIFY BY EAR, first: thumb level against the fingers (0.60 / 0.56 / 0.49 against 0.53 / 0.46) and its length (0.9 of a beat, no

* Sections and the Band menus: the menus are supreme -- 2026-10-10
User: with per-section styles "I can't make edits on the fly through the menus on the page. Those should always be supreme."
Before this the menus did NOT follow a section's style (the user believed they did); the section's style silently won over them.
- Player and BandMidi.generate: opts.sectionOverrides = { section index: options }. A section listed there is played with those options
  laid over the page's, and its %%style from the chart is not consulted (bar opts carry sectionStyle "menus").
- Page (tools/_backing-track.qmd, "Sections and the Band menus"): when a section starts to sound, the Band menus change to its settings:
  what was last set for it here, else its %%style (styleState: the style plus any single parts named after it, unlocking the menus
  when a part does not fit), else the tune's own. A change made while a section's settings show is kept for that section (secOv);
  in a section with no style of its own it changes the tune's settings, as before. The tune's own settings are kept underneath (secBase).
- Hold: going round one section does not touch the menus (same section index = nothing happens).
- Under Next section: a line saying whose settings the menus show; 'Apply to every "Chorus" (n)' copies the menus to every section whose
  name is the same once trailing numbers are dropped (Chorus, Chorus 2); "Back to the chart's settings" forgets the change to this section.
- What counts as a section's settings (SEC_KEYS): instrument and sound, rhythm and blend, voicings and blend, voicing movement, extensions,
  bass line, bass sound, walk amount, groove, cymbal, feel, push, time feel, boom-chick strength, second instrument. Everything else
  (stops, fills, chorus bars, pins, variation, tempo, mixer) belongs to the tune.
- A chart whose sections change (names, lengths or styles) drops every kept change. Tests: styles/t_override.js, styles/menus.cdp.js.
- Also fixed: the page's MIDI export left the second chord instrument out (it named its three parts); it now goes with the first.

* Section settings saved in a setup, by section name -- 2026-10-10
User: starting from a ChordPro song, opening it in the Backing Track and designing the band section by section, the result must be savable.
- A saved setup gains =sections: [{ name, nth, opts, state, sounds }]=: one entry per section changed in the menus. name + nth (which of
  the sections with that name, from 0) is the key, NOT the bar or section number. opts = what the player is given (sectionOverrides),
  state = the menus, sounds = the sample sets it needs.
- BandCatalog.nameSections / placeSections put them back on a chart by name. A section whose own nth was not saved takes that name's
  settings only if every saved section of the name has the same ones (so a song that gains a fourth chorus gives it the choruses' settings).
  A renamed section loses its settings; names are compared without case.
- Saving while a section's settings show now saves the tune's own settings as the setup's (they are kept underneath), not the section's.
- Lyrics site (~/Projects/carols): nothing new to do in the song file. Save the setup, "Download all", keep it beside the song as
  <song>.band.json (tools/chordpro.py passes =sections= through untouched). The Backing Track window gets the whole setup and places it
  on the song's sections; site/band.html (the band on the song page itself) does the same through sectionSetup(), while the setup's own
  style is the one chosen there.
